Inscriptions: "Fu" in vermilion, "Baoshi's work of winning the heart" and "often after getting drunk" in vermilion.　　In the picture, the river level is like a mirror. In the boat near the shore, the scribe sleeps on the piano after getting drunk, with a scroll spread out on the prow of the boat and a wine glass and a wine jug resting on the stern. A bay of clear water and a pine tree are a true depiction of the mentality of the scholar who is far away from the hustle and bustle of the world and is swimming in the forest.　　The "Jiangdong Cloth" is the late Ming and early Qing Dynasty painter Cheng Shen, who had an influence on Fu Baoshi's early painting. I don't know how many times I have painted it, but I have never found one that I am very satisfied with. The one on display is the most recent one, and the one I think is barely tenable. My difficulty is of course due to my lack of skill and breadth of mind, and my inability to catch up with the goal I want to achieve.
